question_stem: A car has mass $1000 \text{ kg}$. When the car is travelling at a steady speed of $v \text{ m s}^{-1}$, where $v > 2$, the resistance to motion of the car is $(Av + B) \text{ N}$, where $A$ and $B$ are constants. The car can travel along a horizontal road at a steady speed of $18 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ when its engine is working at $36 \text{ kW}$. The car can travel up a hill inclined at an angle of $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin \theta = 0.05$, at a steady speed of $12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ when its engine is working at $21 \text{ kW}$.
